title: You thought the silence meant God said no.
paragraphs: You thought the silence meant God said no.
That the closed doors, the unanswered prayers, the years that didn’t look like anything you imagined… meant you were forgotten.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God does some of His deepest work in delays you don’t understand.
And all of it happened after God gave him a dream.
That’s the part that stings, isn’t it?
Because you can handle waiting… but waiting after you’ve seen what God promised? That feels like cruelty.
Joseph had the dream. You’ve had moments like that too. A glimpse. A calling. A conviction that wouldn’t leave you.
And then everything went the opposite direction.
When you were doing right and life still went wrong.
You knew something wasn’t adding up between what God showed you and what you were living.
And that tension… that’s where many people quietly walk away.
Joseph’s story didn’t break in the pit.
It didn’t end in the prison.
Years later, standing face to face with the very people who destroyed his life, Joseph says something that sounds impossible unless God was real every second of the delay:
“In Genesis 50:20 — ‘You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good…’”
God is not scrambling to repair it.
Every moment you thought you were falling behind…
But here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
He was being changed in it.
Because if God gave you everything when you first asked…
you would carry pride instead of purpose.
You would mishandle what was meant to bless others.
You would worship the gift instead of the Giver.
And some of you don’t like that answer.
But delay exposes what you actually trust.
If your faith dies in waiting…
was it faith in God, or faith in outcomes?
Joseph didn’t become a ruler in Egypt overnight.
He became a man God could trust with influence.
And that’s where this cuts deep.
Because some of what you’re calling “delay”…
is God refusing to release you into something your character can’t carry yet.
But there’s another layer you can’t ignore.
Because even Joseph couldn’t save souls.
but he couldn’t deal with sin.
And it looked like the ultimate delay…
as He hung on a cross.
was actually God’s greatest plan unfolding.
Three days later, the resurrection shattered the lie that silence means denial.
He was working salvation through what looked like suffering.
And now the question turns to you.
What are you doing in your delay?
Because there are only two outcomes here.
You either let delay push you away from God…
or you let it drive you deeper into Him.
And right now, you already feel which direction you’re leaning.
Say it plainly if it’s true…
“I stopped trusting God because it didn’t happen when I wanted.”
That honesty is where change begins.
Don’t keep this to yourself either.
There’s someone you know who is quietly losing faith because life isn’t working out.
Because silence is swallowing people who were once close to God.
And if something in you knows you need more than motivation… you need truth that corrects you, confronts you, and rebuilds you…
Walk deeper with the Gospel Warrior.
There’s more waiting for you than surface-level faith.
